sources.label: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol pricing
sources.note: Comparator generation accounting uses the same conservative upper-bound treatment as Gate 13: every input token at $10/M (long-context $8/M plus the 1.25x cache-write factor) and every output token at $30/M. This can overstate actual spend but avoids a false cost advantage when per-request threshold/cache-write conditions cannot be reconstructed from aggregate Codex usage.

sources.label: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Luna pricing
sources.note: Blinded reviewer accounting uses $0.50/M input (long-context $0.40/M multiplied by the 1.25x cache-write factor) and $1.80/M output (long-context output rate), again as an upper-bound treatment.

sources.label: AWS EC2 t3.2xlarge reference compute
sources.note: Browser/runtime accounting uses the same $0.3328/hour reference-compute allocation as the frozen Gate 13 acceptance packet. This is normalized reference accounting, not a claim that the comparator physically runs on AWS or that Codex usage is billed through the API.
